puzzles.name: Claw Rake of Dead Horse Wash
puzzles.subtitle: the Superstition Range

entry.title: CLAW RAKE OF DEAD HORSE WASH · CASE 001
entry.body: The Claw Rake of Dead Horse Wash was delivered to the society in 1976 by a farmer who would accept no payment, wishing only to be rid of it.

entry.title: THE ADOBE OVEN · CASE 002
entry.body: The Adobe Oven appears in three surveys and is absent from four. All seven were conducted competently. No further survey is planned.

entry.title: THE ABANDONED ARROWHEAD · CASE 003
entry.body: Item logged 1986. Chain of custody: incomplete. Explanation on file: none. Status: unresolved, like the rest of the drawer.

entry.title: BOLO TIE OF BUZZARD POINT · CASE 004
entry.body: It was just sitting there, out past the Mogollon Rim, like it had been left for someone to find. Maybe it was. Maybe that someone was me.

entry.title: THE CRACKED MYSTERY EGG · CASE 005
entry.body: My uncle kept it in a drawer since 1966. Would not say where he got it. After he passed, I found the map it was wrapped in.

puzzles.name: Spiral Petroglyph of the Mogollon Rim
puzzles.subtitle: the Dry Basin

entry.title: SPIRAL PETROGLYPH OF THE MOGOLLON RIM · CASE 006
entry.body: Everyone around Skinwalker Ranch knows the Spiral Petroglyph of the Mogollon Rim. Nobody will give you directions to it. You find it, or it finds you.

entry.title: THE HALF-BURIED SNAKE RATTLE · CASE 007
entry.body: It was just sitting there, out past Rattlesnake Flats, like it had been left for someone to find. Maybe it was. Maybe that someone was me.

entry.title: THE CHILI PEPPER · CASE 008
entry.body: The Chili Pepper was catalogued, photographed, and locked up. The lock has needed replacing twice. No further comment is on record.

entry.title: CLAY OLLA OF SKINWALKER RANCH · CASE 009
entry.body: Our party came upon the Clay Olla of Skinwalker Ranch near the Mogollon Rim, abandoned in circumstances I hesitate to record. We carried it out; none among us would carry it twice.

entry.title: THE HALF-BURIED EVIDENCE TAG · CASE 010
entry.body: Field note: item recovered off the trail past Rattlesnake Flats. Condition inconsistent with time exposed. Recommend cross-reference with prior cases.

entry.title: THE CRACKED WANTED POSTER · CASE 011
entry.body: Let this entry attest that the article was found at Saguaro Draw, untouched by weather in a season of storms. Philosophy offers no account of it.

entry.title: THE THE OBJECT · CASE 012
entry.body: My uncle kept it in a drawer since 1989. Would not say where he got it. After he passed, I found the map it was wrapped in.

entry.title: BRANDING IRON OF THE SUPERSTITION RANGE · CASE 013
entry.body: Field note: item recovered off the trail past the Mogollon Rim. Condition inconsistent with time exposed. Recommend cross-reference with prior cases.

entry.title: SHERIFF BADGE OF BUZZARD POINT · CASE 014
entry.body: One Sheriff Badge of Buzzard Point, recovered at Rattlesnake Flats. No owner came forward. Per policy, unclaimed evidence is destroyed after ninety days. This item has been in storage since 1979.

entry.title: THE COWBOY SPURS · CASE 015
entry.body: The Cowboy Spurs was catalogued, photographed, and locked up. The lock has needed replacing twice. No further comment is on record.

entry.title: THE SCORPION · CASE 016
entry.body: We were near Rattlesnake Flats when the dogs quit barking all at once. That is when I saw it. I have not been back after dark since.

entry.title: THE SILENT TARANTULA · CASE 017
entry.body: A dark shape off Buzzard Point. Three witnesses, one photograph, no clear resolution. The report was filed and, per policy, quietly closed.

entry.title: THE DUST-CAKED CANTEEN · CASE 018
entry.body: Recovered upon the road past Buzzard Point in the year 1985: this curious article, of which no traveller would claim ownership. It is set down here among the evidence.

entry.title: THE HALF-BURIED HORSESHOE · CASE 019
entry.body: We found the Half-Buried Horseshoe on the second day. Whatever left it there had come back through Rattlesnake Flats that same night. The prints went right past our tent.

puzzles.subtitle: the Mesa

entry.title: DESERT BAT OF THE DRY BASIN · CASE 020
entry.body: Observed 2006 near Saguaro Draw. Approximately human height, not human gait. No further comment was offered by the witness or requested of them.

entry.title: THE SOMBRERO · CASE 021
entry.body: Found at the Mogollon Rim: one The Sombrero, owner unknown. No tracks leading in. No tracks leading out. Logged and shelved.

entry.title: THE COWBOY BOOT · CASE 022
entry.body: Recovered upon the road past Skinwalker Ranch in the year 1970: this curious article, of which no traveller would claim ownership. It is set down here among the evidence.

entry.title: THE FERAL HORNED LIZARD · CASE 023
entry.body: It was 1988 and I swore I would never tell anyone. But I know what stood at the edge of the Mogollon Rim, and it was no animal I can name.

puzzles.name: Saguaro Cactus of the Mogollon Rim
puzzles.subtitle: the Mesa

entry.title: SAGUARO CACTUS OF THE MOGOLLON RIM · CASE 024
entry.body: My father drove past the Saguaro Cactus of the Mogollon Rim every day for thirty years. In 1974 he started taking the long way. He never said why.

entry.title: THE LASSO · CASE 025
entry.body: It was just sitting there, out past Dead Horse Wash, like it had been left for someone to find. Maybe it was. Maybe that someone was me.

entry.title: PRICKLY PEAR OF BUZZARD POINT · CASE 026
entry.body: Locals will not camp within sight of the Prickly Pear of Buzzard Point. When asked why, they answer a different question. Noted, 1990; still unexplained.

entry.title: THE DUST-CAKED COYOTE · CASE 027
entry.body: It was 1986 and I swore I would never tell anyone. But I know what stood at the edge of Buzzard Point, and it was no animal I can name.

entry.title: THE GAMBEL'S QUAIL · CASE 028
entry.body: I only saw it for a breath, out past the Superstition Range. It watched me the way a person watches, then stepped back into the dark and was just gone.

entry.title: JACKRABBIT OF SAGUARO DRAW · CASE 029
entry.body: Report from the Superstition Range: a shape too large for any bear, moving without sound. No scat, no den. Witness sober. Logged as Jackrabbit of Saguaro Draw.

entry.title: PICKAXE OF THE MESA · CASE 030
entry.body: I found it half-covered near the Mogollon Rim. Nobody camps out there. Nobody has for years. I brought it back and I still wish I had not.

entry.title: THE COILED RATTLER · CASE 031
entry.body: Field note: heavy sign along the Mogollon Rim. Snapped branches at eight feet. Smell of wet copper. Did not linger to confirm.

entry.title: THE JACKALOPE · CASE 032

entry.title: ARMADILLO OF THE MOGOLLON RIM · CASE 033
entry.body: Sighted near Dead Horse Wash, 1969. Held still at the tree line, then was gone. Tracks pressed deep in wet ground. Recommend the file stay open.

entry.title: THE BANDED GILA MONSTER · CASE 034

entry.title: THE CHUPACABRA · CASE 035

entry.title: THE RED-EYED COILED DIAMONDBACK · CASE 036
entry.body: Duration of sighting: under a minute. Location: the Mesa. Conclusion: inconclusive, which is the only honest word for it.

entry.title: PRAIRIE DOG OF RATTLESNAKE FLATS · CASE 037
entry.body: Our party, encamped near the Superstition Range in the autumn of 2013, observed a figure of uncommon stature. It regarded us without fear, then withdrew as though it had never been.

entry.title: THE CRACKED STAGECOACH · CASE 038
entry.body: Recovered near Rattlesnake Flats, 2006. Bagged, tagged, photographed. Nothing about where it lay makes sense. The file stays open.

entry.title: SKINWALKER OF COYOTE ARROYO · CASE 039

entry.title: BONE WALKER OF BUZZARD POINT · CASE 041

entry.title: THE SILENT FRESNO NIGHTCRAWLER · CASE 042
entry.body: Let the record show that on the road past the Dry Basin, in the year 1978, a thing was seen which philosophy cannot yet explain.

entry.title: MESA STALKER OF SKINWALKER RANCH · CASE 043

entry.title: THE TALL SAGUARO · CASE 045
entry.body: Surveyed Dead Horse Wash, 2013. The Tall Saguaro is on no map of the area, and the county keeps no record of it. It is there all the same.

entry.title: ADOBE PUEBLO OF SAGUARO DRAW · CASE 046
entry.body: Let it be recorded that in 1965 the Adobe Pueblo of Saguaro Draw was observed to stand dark and silent, though every account agrees it had no cause to be either.

entry.title: THE SHIFTING OWLMAN · CASE 049
